text:
Priya: Alert — seeing a sharp uptick in GPU Xid 79 / kernel timeouts across eu-west-1 after yesterday's driver rollout (535.12). Failure rate ~0.6% on gpu-pool-2, NCCL watchdog logs spiking, a handful of pods auto-evicted. Not huge impact yet but trending.

eng-bot: automated alert: [GPU Error Rate] eu-west-1 gpu-pool-2 > threshold (0.5%) — triggered at 1863278420. Incident ID: GPU-1863.

Mike: linking graphs — can you paste the short window of the errors and a histogram of node counts? curious if it's concentrated on a single bin.

Priya: grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd1234/gpu-errors?orgId=1&from=now-2h&to=now — mostly eu-west-1-a and .b, roughly 8 nodes, 2.5x normal NCCL watch timeout events. Logs snippet:

```
May 03 09:12:17 gpu-node-12 kernel: NVRM: Xid (79): GPU has fallen off the bus.
May 03 09:12:18 kubelet: Pod "trainer-x" evicted due to NodeProblem
May 03 09:12:18 kubelet: docker: error response from daemon: containerd: container did not start
May 03 09:12:19 nv_peer_mem: nccl: watchdog timeout at rank 3
```

Anna: OK, triage plan: 1) cordon affected nodes, 2) rollback driver to previous known-good (534.88) on a small canary subset, 3) increase NCCL watchdog timeout as a soft mitigation if rollback takes too long. Who can run the rollback?

Sam: I can run the rollback canary in eu-west-1-a. Runbook steps (short):
1) cordon nodes: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-12`
2) drain low-priority pods: `kubectl drain gpu-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
3) apply driver rollback (daemonset): `kubectl -n kube-system set image daemonset/gpu-driver gpu-driver=registry.redwood/driver:534.88`
4) watch GPU error metric and nv_peer_mem logs for 10m.

Mike: Recommend also capture dmesg + nv_peer_mem logs before we touch them: `journalctl -u kubelet -n 200; dmesg | tail -n 200; sudo cat /var/log/nv_peer_mem.log | tail -n 200` — paste to s3 with `psl` helper: `psl upload /tmp/node12-logs.tar.gz s3://redwood-uploads/GPU-1863/`

Priya: FYI cost/impact: if we drain 8 nodes we can shift non-critical workloads but high-throughput jobs may backfill elsewhere causing spot/egress cost spike. Keep migrations limited to canaries.

eng-bot: pagerduty: firing for GPU-1863 — escalation step 1.

Anna: Action items: @Sam will run canary rollback in eu-west-1-a now, @Mike will gather logs and update the dashboard with an Xid-code breakdown panel, @Priya will coordinate customer-impact comms if we hit 1% error rate. I'll standby to expand rollback to .b after canary green.

Sam: starting canary rollback — cordoning node-12 and node-15 now.

Mike: uploading logs to s3, collecting histograms. will also add an alert rule to split Xid by code.

Priya: if canary shows reduction in Xid 79 within 10–15m we proceed to roll forward rollback to remaining affected nodes, else escalate to kernel-level debug (collect kernel stacks + nv-hostengine traces).

Anna: note for postmortem: add driver compatibility test to our pre-rollout suite for the specific kernel version in eu-west (kernel 5.15.0-azure) — avoid this blind spot. Also track total cost delta when we re-schedule training jobs (for later root-cause analysis).

Sam: canary rollback completed on node-12, node-15 — initial metrics: Xid 79 events down ~70% in the last 8 minutes. Monitoring for 30m.

Priya: good signal. proceeding to roll remaining 6 nodes in small batches. will update when complete.

Mike: updating alert thresholds to reduce noisy paging — new rule: if Xid rate > 1% for 10m then page, else create ticket. will backfill historical Xid code panel.

eng-bot: automated note: GPU-1863 mitigation in progress, status: partial rollback canary success.

Anna: closing note: after stabilization, schedule a kernel+driver compatibility matrix run in our staging fleet and add unit E2E that exercises NCCL allreduce in canary gauge. Postmortem owner: Priya. Timeline: 24–48h.

Priya: thanks team — monitoring and will post final update when all affected nodes are back on 534.88 or we have deeper diagnostics. :thumbsup:
